q: Left ventricle fails in this recap. Where does blood back up?

opts.why: The left side receives from the lungs. Fail the left ventricle and fluid is pushed into the alveoli: crackles, shortness of breath, pink frothy sputum.
Body backup is right-sided failure: JVD and dependent edema.
Vena cava backup is the right-sided path, not left ventricle failure.
Leg edema is a right-sided backup. Left failure backs up into the lungs.

q: Right ventricle fails in this recap. What finding fits?

opts.why: The right side receives from the body. Fail it and blood backs up into the vena cava: JVD and dependent edema (legs or sacrum).
Lung backup is left-sided failure, not right ventricle failure.
Crushing pressure is the MI picture. Right failure is JVD and dependent edema.
Pain that eases with rest is stable angina, not right-sided backup.

q: What does myocardial infarction mean in this recap?

opts.why: MI is death of cardiac muscle cells. Dead cells do not come back. Save the tissue around them that is not dead yet.
Low flow with cells still alive is ischemia, not infarction.
Plaque is atherosclerosis. Infarction is cell death after ischemia lasts long enough.
A clot on plaque is how the block grows. Infarction is cell death after ischemia lasts long enough.

q: Unstable angina in this recap. What is changing?

opts.why: Unstable angina is a changing pattern: less work than usual, pain at rest, longer pain, or more nitro than usual.
Same work every time is stable angina, not a changing pattern.
Easing in 3 to 8 minutes is the stable picture. Unstable is the pattern changing.
Usual nitro still working is stable. Unstable needs more nitro or does not respond.

q: Aspirin dose in this recap, if they have taken none?

opts.why: Two to four baby aspirins of 81 mg each, total 162 to 324 mg, chewed. Four is common if they have taken none.
0.4 mg under the tongue is nitroglycerin, not aspirin.
81 mg is one baby tablet, not the full dose, and this recap wants it chewed.
This recap wants the aspirin chewed, not swallowed whole.

q: Before each nitro dose in this recap, systolic pressure must be at least what?

opts.why: Confirm systolic pressure of at least 100 mmHg before each nitro dose. Recheck after each dose.
90 mmHg is the CPAP floor in this recap, not the nitro floor.
94 percent is the oxygen-sat floor, not the nitro pressure floor.
You check pressure before every nitro dose, not once.

q: Recent erectile-dysfunction meds. Nitro in this recap?

opts.why: No recent erectile-dysfunction meds (Viagra, Cialis, Levitra) in the last 24 to 48 hours.
Five minutes is the gap between nitro doses, not the erectile-dysfunction window.
Good pressure does not cancel the erectile-dysfunction hold.

opts.t: Hold only if pain is gone
opts.why: Still having pain is a nitro yes. Erectile-dysfunction meds are still a no.

q: Which rhythms does this recap say the AED shocks?

opts.why: Shockable rhythms are ventricular fibrillation and ventricular tachycardia. Pulseless VT is treated the same as VF.
The AED shock for VT in this recap is pulseless VT, same as VF.
SA node at 60 to 100 is the normal pacemaker, not a shockable arrest rhythm.
AV delay is normal conduction. The AED shocks VF and pulseless VT.

q: Adult CPR depth in this recap?

opts.why: Adult depth is at least 2 inches. Child is about 2 inches. Infant is about 1.5 inches.
1.5 inches is the infant depth, not the adult depth.
About 2 inches is the child depth. Adult is at least 2 inches.
One-third chest is the child/infant rule. Adult depth is at least 2 inches.

q: CPAP for left-sided failure in this recap. Lowest systolic?

opts.why: CPAP if they are conscious, breathing adequately, and systolic pressure is at least 90, with no major vomiting or trauma.
100 mmHg is the nitro floor in this recap, not the CPAP floor.
94 percent is the oxygen-sat floor, not the CPAP pressure floor.
CPAP still needs a systolic of at least 90, not a one-time skip.
Aim for SpO2 94 to 99 percent. Device depends on rate, rhythm, and quality of breathing.
This recap target is 94 to 99 percent, not 100 every time.
90 to 93 is below this recap’s 94 to 99 percent target.
The target is the band 94 to 99 percent, not a single 94.

q: Cardiogenic shock in this recap. How do you position them?

opts.why: Shock wins over sitting up. Lie them supine unless they absolutely cannot breathe lying down.
Sitting up is for chest pain with a stable pressure, not for shock.
Extra pillows and sitting up are the PND/CHF positions, not cardiogenic shock.
If they cannot breathe lying down, do not force them flat. Shock still usually wants supine.
